+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Peer-memory transport for the cross-rank "push" kernels.
+
+Every cross-rank exchange of the specialized decode is a push: a producer
+kernel stores its partial (Lamport-tagged words) straight into each peer's
+receive buffer through a device pointer, and the consumer polls its own
+buffer. The kernels only need, per exchange buffer, the local base pointer
+and every rank's base pointer (`peer_ptrs[rank] == local`). How those
+pointers are obtained is this module's job, behind `PeerTransport`:
+
+- `IpcPeerTransport` (default, TP <= 8 inside one NVLink domain of a single
+  OS instance, e.g. the 4 GPUs of a GB200/GB300 tray): one plain
+  `cudaMalloc` arena per rank, CUDA IPC handles all-gathered once over the
+  CPU group, peers opened once. Uses vLLM's `CudaRTLibrary`.
+- `SymmMemPeerTransport` (TP <= 16, one NVLink domain, any number of OS
+  instances, e.g. TP8/16 over the trays of a GB200/GB300 NVL72): torch
+  symmetric memory, the mechanism vLLM's M3 `finalize_allreduce_norm` and
+  `SymmMemCommunicator` already use. Across nodes torch maps the peers
+  through fabric (multi-node NVLink) handles; the arena also gets an NVLS
+  multicast address when the fabric supports it. The kernels do not change,
+  only the provider of `peer_ptrs`.
+
+`make_transport("auto", ...)` picks CUDA IPC when every rank of the group is
+on this node and symmetric memory otherwise.
+
+`MAX_PEERS` is the peer table of the device structs (`int* p[16]`): every
+transport serves up to 16 ranks (CUDA IPC up to 8, one node). A buffer's
+`mc_ptr` is its NVLS multicast address (0 without one): one store there lands
+at the same offset in every rank's buffer, which is what the push protocol's
+multicast mode (`_exchange.PushWorkspace.multicast`) uses.
+
+Buffers are carved from one arena per transport, in the same order on every
+rank (the allocation calls are collective by construction: every rank builds
+the same stages in the same order).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ctypes
+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    import torch
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+MAX_PEERS = 16  # the device structs hold ``int* p[16]`` (TP16: four NVL72 trays)
+MAX_TRANSPORT_PEERS = MAX_PEERS
+MAX_IPC_PEERS = 8  # one node
+TRANSPORT_KINDS = ("auto", "cuda_ipc", "symm_mem", "loopback")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PeerBuffer:
+    name: str
+    nbytes: int
+    rank: int
+    world: int
+    local: torch.Tensor  # torch.uint8 CUDA tensor over this rank's buffer
+    peer_ptrs: tuple[int, ...]  # every rank's base address, [rank] is local
+    _dev: torch.Tensor | None = field(default=None, repr=False)
+    mc_ptr: int = 0  # NVLS multicast address of the buffer (0: none)
+
+    def peer_ptrs_tensor(self, table: int = MAX_PEERS):
+        """int64 [table] on the device (zero padded), for kernels that take
+        the peer table by pointer."""
+        import torch
+
+        if self._dev is None or self._dev.numel() != table:
+            v = self.peer_ptrs_padded(table)
+            self._dev = torch.tensor(v, dtype=torch.int64, device=self.local.device)
+        return self._dev
+
+    def peer_ptrs_padded(self, table: int = MAX_PEERS) -> list[int]:
+        """Every rank's address, zero padded to a device peer table of
+        `table` entries; raises if the world does not fit."""
+        if len(self.peer_ptrs) > table:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{self.name}: world {len(self.peer_ptrs)} exceeds the device "
+                f"peer table ({table})"
+            )
+        return list(self.peer_ptrs) + [0] * (table - len(self.peer_ptrs))
+
+
+def _align(x: int, a: int) -> int:
+    return (x + a - 1) // a * a
+
+
+class PeerMemoryError(RuntimeError):
+    """Peer memory could not be set up on some rank; raised on every rank
+    of the group at the same point (`PeerTransport.agree`)."""
+
+
+class PeerTransport(ABC):
+    """Hands out peer-addressable buffers for one TP group."""
+
+    kind: str = "abstract"
+    max_world: int = MAX_TRANSPORT_PEERS
+
+    def __init__(self, rank: int, world: int, capacity: int):
+        if not 1 <= world <= self.max_world:
+            raise ValueError(f"{self.kind}: world {world} outside 1..{self.max_world}")
+        self.rank, self.world, self.capacity = rank, world, capacity
+        self._used = 0
+        self._bufs: dict[str, PeerBuffer] = {}
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def _base_ptrs(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+        """Every rank's arena base (collective on first call)."""
+
+    def agree(self, ok: bool, what: str) -> None:
+        """Collective: raise `PeerMemoryError` on every rank if `ok` is
+        false on any rank. Every rank calls it at the same point, so a local
+        failure never leaves the peers waiting in a later collective."""
+        if not ok:
+            raise PeerMemoryError(f"{what} failed")
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def _local_tensor(self):
+        """This rank's arena as a uint8 CUDA tensor."""
+
+    def alloc(self, name: str, nbytes: int, align: int = 256) -> PeerBuffer:
+        """A zero-initialized buffer at the same arena offset on every rank."""
+        if name in self._bufs:
+            b = self._bufs[name]
+            if b.nbytes != nbytes:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"{name}: re-requested with {nbytes} B, had {b.nbytes}"
+                )
+            return b
+        off = _align(self._used, align)
+        if off + nbytes > self.capacity:
+            raise MemoryError(
+                f"peer arena ({self.kind}) exhausted: {name} needs {nbytes} B at "
+                f"{off}, capacity {self.capacity} B"
+            )
+        self._used = off + nbytes
+        bases = self._base_ptrs()
+        local = self._local_tensor().narrow(0, off, nbytes)
+        local.zero_()
+        mc = self.multicast_ptr
+        b = PeerBuffer(
+            name,
+            nbytes,
+            self.rank,
+            self.world,
+            local,
+            tuple(p + off for p in bases),
+            mc_ptr=mc + off if mc else 0,
+        )
+        self._bufs[name] = b
+        return b
+
+    @property
+    def multicast_ptr(self) -> int:
+        """The arena's multicast base address (0: the transport has none)."""
+        return 0
+
+    def barrier(self) -> None:
+        """Wait for every rank (a no-op for a one-rank transport)."""
+        return None
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        """Release the arena (nothing to release by default)."""
+        return None
+
+
+def _wrap_ptr(ptr: int, nbytes: int, device: int):
+    import torch
+
+    class _Buf:
+        __cuda_array_interface__ = {
+            "shape": (nbytes,),
+            "typestr": "|u1",
+            "data": (ptr, False),
+            "version": 3,
+        }
+
+    return torch.as_tensor(_Buf(), device=f"cuda:{device}")
+
+
+class IpcPeerTransport(PeerTransport):
+    """CUDA IPC over one plain cudaMalloc arena (single-node TP only)."""
+
+    kind = "cuda_ipc"
+    max_world = MAX_IPC_PEERS
+
+    def __init__(self, cpu_group, rank: int, world: int, capacity: int):
+        super().__init__(rank, world, capacity)
+        self._group = cpu_group
+        self._lib: Any = None
+        self._base = 0
+        self._bases: tuple[int, ...] | None = None
+        self._opened: list[int] = []
+        self._tensor: torch.Tensor | None = None
+
+    def _ensure(self):
+        if self._bases is not None:
+            return
+        import torch
+        import torch.distributed as dist
+
+        from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.cuda_wrapper import (
+            CudaRTLibrary,
+            cudaIpcMemHandle_t,
+        )
+
+        dev = torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+        self._lib = lib = CudaRTLibrary()
+        # Every rank takes part in both exchanges below even if its local step failed
+        # (None / False marks the failure), so all ranks raise together.
+        h = None
+        try:
+            p = lib.cudaMalloc(max(self.capacity, 1))
+            self._base = int(p.value)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+            lib.cudaMemset(p, 0, max(self.capacity, 1))
+            h = bytes(lib.cudaIpcGetMemHandle(p))
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("peer arena: allocation failed on rank %d", self.rank)
+        hs: list = [None] * self.world
+        dist.all_gather_object(hs, h, group=self._group)
+        if any(x is None for x in hs):
+            self.close()
+            raise PeerMemoryError("peer arena allocation failed on some rank")
+        bases: list[int] = []
+        try:
+            for r, hb in enumerate(hs):
+                if r == self.rank:
+                    bases.append(self._base)
+                    continue
+                q = lib.cudaIpcOpenMemHandle(cudaIpcMemHandle_t.from_buffer_copy(hb))
+                self._opened.append(int(q.value))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+                bases.append(int(q.value))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+            opened = True
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception(
+                "peer arena: opening the peers failed on rank %d", self.rank
+            )
+            opened = False
+        oks: list = [None] * self.world
+        dist.all_gather_object(oks, opened, group=self._group)
+        if not all(oks):
+            self.close()
+            raise PeerMemoryError("opening the peer arenas failed on some rank")
+        self._bases = tuple(bases)
+        self._tensor = _wrap_ptr(self._base, self.capacity, dev)
+
+    def _base_ptrs(self):
+        self._ensure()
+        return self._bases
+
+    def _local_tensor(self):
+        self._ensure()
+        return self._tensor
+
+    def barrier(self) -> None:
+        import torch.distributed as dist
+
+        dist.barrier(group=self._group)
+
+    def agree(self, ok: bool, what: str) -> None:
+        import torch.distributed as dist
+
+        oks: list = [None] * self.world
+        dist.all_gather_object(oks, bool(ok), group=self._group)
+        if not all(oks):
+            raise PeerMemoryError(f"{what} failed on some rank")
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        if self._lib is None:
+            return
+        import torch
+
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        close = self._lib.lib.cudaIpcCloseMemHandle
+        close.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]
+        for q in self._opened:
+            close(ctypes.c_void_p(q))
+        if self._base:
+            self._lib.cudaFree(ctypes.c_void_p(self._base))
+        self._opened, self._lib, self._bases, self._tensor = [], None, None, None
+        self._base = 0
+
+
+class SymmMemPeerTransport(PeerTransport):
+    """torch symmetric memory over the TP device group (single or multi node).
+
+    One `symm_mem.empty` arena per rank, rendezvoused once over `group`
+    (a `ProcessGroup` or its name). Within one OS instance torch maps the
+    peers with CUDA IPC (POSIX fd) handles; across the trays of an NVL72 it
+    uses fabric handles, which need the IMEX channel in the container
+    (`/dev/nvidia-caps-imex-channels`). `multicast_ptr` is the arena's
+    NVLS multicast address (0 when the fabric does not provide one), at the
+    same offsets as `peer_ptrs`."""
+
+    kind = "symm_mem"
+
+    def __init__(self, group, rank: int, world: int, capacity: int):
+        super().__init__(rank, world, capacity)
+        self._group = group
+        self._buf: Any = None
+        self._handle: Any = None
+
+    def _ensure(self):
+        if self._handle is not None:
+            return
+        import torch
+        import torch.distributed._symmetric_memory as symm_mem
+
+        group = self._group
+        name = group if isinstance(group, str) else group.group_name
+        enable = getattr(symm_mem, "enable_symm_mem_for_group", None)
+        if enable is not None:  # a no-op (or absent) on newer torch
+            enable(name)
+        # Every rank agrees before and after the rendezvous (a collective), so a local
+        # failure raises on every rank instead of leaving peers in it.
+        buf = None
+        try:
+            buf = symm_mem.empty(
+                max(self.capacity, 1),
+                dtype=torch.uint8,
+                device=torch.accelerator.current_device_index(),
+            )
+            buf.zero_()
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception("symm_mem arena: allocation failed on rank %d", self.rank)
+        self.agree(buf is not None, "symm_mem arena allocation")
+        handle = symm_mem.rendezvous(buf, name)
+        # peer_ptrs / multicast_ptr are the allocation's bases: the arena must start
+        # there (a pooled sub-allocation would not).
+        ok = (
+            int(handle.buffer_ptrs[self.rank]) == int(buf.data_ptr())  # type: ignore[union-attr]
+            and handle.world_size == self.world
+            and handle.rank == self.rank
+        )
+        if not ok:
+            logger.error(
+                "symm_mem rendezvous on rank %d: base %#x vs allocation %#x, "
+                "rank %d/%d, expected %d/%d",
+                self.rank,
+                int(handle.buffer_ptrs[self.rank]),
+                int(buf.data_ptr()),  # type: ignore[union-attr]
+                handle.rank,
+                handle.world_size,
+                self.rank,
+                self.world,
+            )
+        self.agree(ok, "symm_mem rendezvous")
+        self._buf, self._handle = buf, handle
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        handle.barrier()
+
+    def _process_group(self):
+        if not isinstance(self._group, str):
+            return self._group
+        from torch.distributed.distributed_c10d import _resolve_process_group
+
+        return _resolve_process_group(self._group)
+
+    def agree(self, ok: bool, what: str) -> None:
+        import torch
+        import torch.distributed as dist
+
+        flag = torch.tensor(
+            [1 if ok else 0],
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device=torch.accelerator.current_device_index(),
+        )
+        dist.all_reduce(flag, op=dist.ReduceOp.MIN, group=self._process_group())
+        if not int(flag.item()):
+            raise PeerMemoryError(f"{what} failed on some rank")
+
+    def _base_ptrs(self):
+        self._ensure()
+        return tuple(int(p) for p in self._handle.buffer_ptrs)
+
+    def _local_tensor(self):
+        self._ensure()
+        return self._buf
+
+    @property
+    def multicast_ptr(self) -> int:
+        self._ensure()
+        return int(self._handle.multicast_ptr or 0)
+
+    def barrier(self) -> None:
+        self._ensure()
+        self._handle.barrier()
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        if self._handle is None:
+            return
+        import torch
+
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        self._buf, self._handle = None, None
+
+
+class LoopbackTransport(PeerTransport):
+    """world == 1 (single-GPU kernel tests): the only peer is self."""
+
+    kind = "loopback"
+    max_world = 1
+
+    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
+        super().__init__(0, 1, capacity)
+        self._tensor: Any = None
+
+    def _ensure(self):
+        if self._tensor is None:
+            import torch
+
+            self._tensor = torch.zeros(
+                max(self.capacity, 1), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"
+            )
+
+    def _base_ptrs(self):
+        self._ensure()
+        return (int(self._tensor.data_ptr()),)
+
+    def _local_tensor(self):
+        self._ensure()
+        return self._tensor
+
+
+def all_ranks_on_this_node(cpu_group) -> bool:
+    """Collective over `cpu_group` (gloo): every rank shares this host."""
+    import torch.distributed as dist
+
+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import in_the_same_node_as
+
+    if dist.get_world_size(group=cpu_group) == 1:
+        return True
+    return all(in_the_same_node_as(cpu_group, source_rank=0))
+
+
+def resolve_transport_kind(kind: str, *, cpu_group=None, world: int = 1) -> str:
+    """`auto` -> `loopback` (world 1), `cuda_ipc` (one node, world <=
+    `MAX_IPC_PEERS`) or `symm_mem`. Collective over `cpu_group` for
+    `auto` with world > 1."""
+    if kind not in TRANSPORT_KINDS:
+        raise ValueError(f"unknown peer transport {kind!r}; one of {TRANSPORT_KINDS}")
+    if kind != "auto":
+        return kind
+    if world == 1:
+        return "loopback"
+    if world <= MAX_IPC_PEERS and all_ranks_on_this_node(cpu_group):
+        return "cuda_ipc"
+    return "symm_mem"
+
+
+def make_transport(
+    kind: str,
+    *,
+    group=None,
+    cpu_group=None,
+    rank: int,
+    world: int,
+    capacity: int,
+) -> PeerTransport:
+    """`group`: the device (NCCL) process group, for `symm_mem`;
+    `cpu_group`: its gloo twin, for `cuda_ipc` and `auto`."""
+    kind = resolve_transport_kind(kind, cpu_group=cpu_group, world=world)
+    if kind == "cuda_ipc":
+        return IpcPeerTransport(cpu_group, rank, world, capacity)
+    if kind == "symm_mem":
+        return SymmMemPeerTransport(group, rank, world, capacity)
+    return LoopbackTransport(capacity)
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "MAX_IPC_PEERS",
+    "PeerMemoryError",
+    "MAX_PEERS",
+    "MAX_TRANSPORT_PEERS",
+    "TRANSPORT_KINDS",
+    "all_ranks_on_this_node",
+    "resolve_transport_kind",
+    "IpcPeerTransport",
+    "LoopbackTransport",
+    "PeerBuffer",
+    "PeerTransport",
+    "SymmMemPeerTransport",
+    "make_transport",
+]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Cache-format checks shared by every stage that reads or writes the KV
+cache or the indexer K cache.
+
+The kernels are parametrized by a `CacheFormat` (a compile-time
+parameter of the CuTe DSL kernels). Only `FP8_E4M3` has device code today; `BF16`
+is a declared format with no kernel instantiation yet, so selecting it is
+refused with a clear message instead of silently reinterpreting bytes.
+
+NVFP4 caches are rejected explicitly: an nvfp4 cache is stored as uint8 with
+element size 1, the same as fp8, so a size-only check would accept it and the
+kernels would read 4-bit codes as e4m3.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import enum
+
+
+class CacheFormat(enum.Enum):
+    FP8_E4M3 = "fp8_e4m3"
+    BF16 = "bf16"  # declared; no kernel instantiation yet
+
+
+# Formats with device code in this package.
+IMPLEMENTED_FORMATS = frozenset({CacheFormat.FP8_E4M3})
+
+_KV_NAMES = {
+    "fp8": CacheFormat.FP8_E4M3,
+    "fp8_e4m3": CacheFormat.FP8_E4M3,
+    "auto": CacheFormat.BF16,  # upstream MiniMax M3 default
+    "bfloat16": CacheFormat.BF16,
+    "bf16": CacheFormat.BF16,
+}
+_INDEXER_NAMES = {
+    "fp8": CacheFormat.FP8_E4M3,
+    "auto": CacheFormat.BF16,  # upstream MiniMax M3 default
+    "bf16": CacheFormat.BF16,
+}
+
+
+class CacheDtypeError(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+def _resolve(kind: str, name: str, table: dict) -> CacheFormat:
+    n = str(name).lower()
+    if "nvfp4" in n or "fp4" in n:
+        raise CacheDtypeError(
+            f"{kind} cache dtype {name!r}: NVFP4/FP4 caches are not supported by "
+            "the MiniMax-M3 specialized decode kernels (they read fp8 e4m3)"
+        )
+    fmt = table.get(n)
+    if fmt is None:
+        raise CacheDtypeError(f"{kind} cache dtype {name!r} is not supported")
+    if fmt not in IMPLEMENTED_FORMATS:
+        raise CacheDtypeError(
+            f"{kind} cache dtype {name!r} ({fmt.value}) has no kernel "
+            "instantiation yet; run with fp8 or use the stock decode"
+        )
+    return fmt
+
+
+def kv_cache_format(cache_dtype: str) -> CacheFormat:
+    """From `CacheConfig.cache_dtype`."""
+    return _resolve("KV", cache_dtype, _KV_NAMES)
+
+
+def indexer_cache_format(indexer_kv_dtype: str) -> CacheFormat:
+    """From `AttentionConfig.indexer_kv_dtype` (before 'auto' resolution
+    is fine: 'auto' maps to the model default bf16)."""
+    return _resolve("indexer K", indexer_kv_dtype, _INDEXER_NAMES)
+
+
+def check_cache_tensor(kind: str, t, fmt: CacheFormat) -> None:
+    """Runtime tensor check: the view the kernels get must match `fmt`."""
+    import torch
+
+    ok = {
+        CacheFormat.FP8_E4M3: (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.uint8),
+        CacheFormat.BF16: (torch.bfloat16,),
+    }[fmt]
+    if t.dtype not in ok:
+        raise CacheDtypeError(
+            f"{kind} cache tensor dtype {t.dtype} does not match {fmt.value}"
+        )
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "IMPLEMENTED_FORMATS",
+    "CacheDtypeError",
+    "CacheFormat",
+    "check_cache_tensor",
+    "indexer_cache_format",
+    "kv_cache_format",
+]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The boundary push exchange shared by producers and consumers.
+
+Producers (o_proj GEMV, fused MoE engine) push their bf16 TP-partial rows into
+every rank's exchange (the o_proj / MoE CuTe DSL kernels' push: one 16-byte chunk per
+(row, 8 columns));
+the next boundary consumer (the post kernel after o_proj, the next layer's
+front after the MoE engine) polls its own copy, sums ranks in rank order and
+re-arms the slots with the empty sentinel. One exchange per row bucket.
+
+Layout (int32 words), identical on every rank::
+
+    exch[2 sets][2 parities][maxt][world][H / 2]   bf16x2 words, kEmpty = 0x80000000
+    flags[maxt][cluster]                           local only: per (row, column
+                                                   slice) call parity, flipped by
+                                                   the consumer
+
+`PushParams` (160 bytes: peers[16], flags, rank, world, maxt, cluster, ndst)
+is packed here; the post's host (`post/host.py`) unpacks the same bytes.
+
+Multicast mode: when the transport gives the exchange an NVLS multicast
+address, a producer stores each chunk once, to `mc_ptr` + slot (`peers[0]`
+= the multicast address, `ndst` = 1), and the fabric delivers it to the same
+slot of every rank; the unicast mode stores it `world` times. Consumers do
+not change (they poll and re-arm their local copy). `multicast_policy`
+picks the mode per exchange: multicast when it is available and the group
+spans more than 4 ranks or the bucket is above 8 rows (unicast fan-out
+costs world stores per chunk; NVLS one).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import struct
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+from ._comm import MAX_PEERS, PeerBuffer, PeerTransport
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    import torch
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+HIDDEN = 6144
+K_EMPTY = -0x80000000  # int32 0x80000000: two bf16 -0.0 halves
+BUCKETS = (8, 16)  # row buckets: up to 8 rows, and up to 16
+CLUSTER = 4  # exact-mode column slices per row
+PUSH_PARAMS_FMT = (
+    f"<{MAX_PEERS}qq5i"  # peers[16], flags, rank, world, maxt, cluster, ndst
+)
+PUSH_PARAMS_BYTES = 160  # the packed PushParams struct with 8-byte tail padding
+MULTICAST_MIN_WORLD = 5  # multicast from TP8 up ...
+MULTICAST_MIN_MAXT = 16  # ... or for buckets above 8 rows
+
+
+def multicast_policy(world: int, maxt: int, available: bool) -> bool:
+    """Whether an exchange of `world` ranks and bucket `maxt` pushes
+    through its multicast address (the same answer on every rank)."""
+    if not available or world == 1:
+        return False
+    return world >= MULTICAST_MIN_WORLD or maxt >= MULTICAST_MIN_MAXT
+
+
+def bucket(rows: int) -> int:
+    for b in BUCKETS:
+        if rows <= b:
+            return b
+    raise ValueError(f"rows {rows} exceed the largest exchange bucket {BUCKETS[-1]}")
+
+
+def exchange_words(world: int, maxt: int) -> int:
+    return 4 * maxt * world * (HIDDEN // 2)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PushWorkspace:
+    maxt: int
+    exch: PeerBuffer
+    flags: torch.Tensor  # torch.int32 [maxt * CLUSTER], local
+    multicast: bool = False  # producers push once, through exch.mc_ptr
+
+    @property
+    def rank(self) -> int:
+        return self.exch.rank
+
+    @property
+    def world(self) -> int:
+        return self.exch.world
+
+    @property
+    def ndst(self) -> int:
+        """Destinations of one push: 1 (multicast) or world (unicast)."""
+        return 1 if self.multicast else self.world
+
+    def push_ptrs(self) -> list[int]:
+        """The `ndst` addresses a producer stores each chunk to."""
+        if self.multicast:
+            if not self.exch.mc_ptr:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"{self.exch.name}: multicast without a multicast address"
+                )
+            return [int(self.exch.mc_ptr)]
+        return [int(p) for p in self.exch.peer_ptrs]
+
+    def params_bytes(self) -> bytes:
+        dst = self.push_ptrs()
+        b = struct.pack(
+            PUSH_PARAMS_FMT,
+            *(dst + [0] * (MAX_PEERS - len(dst))),
+            int(self.flags.data_ptr()),
+            self.rank,
+            self.world,
+            self.maxt,
+            CLUSTER,
+            self.ndst,
+        )
+        return b + b"\0" * (PUSH_PARAMS_BYTES - len(b))
+
+    def params_tensor(self):
+        import torch
+
+        return torch.frombuffer(
+            bytearray(self.params_bytes()), dtype=torch.uint8
+        ).clone()
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        """Re-arm (never during graph capture): every slot empty, parity 0."""
+        self.exch.local.view(dtype=_i32()).fill_(K_EMPTY)
+        self.flags.zero_()
+
+
+def _i32():
+    import torch
+
+    return torch.int32
+
+
+def push_workspace(
+    transport: PeerTransport, maxt: int, tag: str = "g3", multicast: bool | None = None
+) -> PushWorkspace:
+    """The bucket-`maxt` exchange (allocated once per transport and tag).
+    `multicast`: the push mode (None: `multicast_policy`); fixed by the
+    first call for a (tag, maxt)."""
+    import torch
+
+    if maxt not in BUCKETS:
+        raise ValueError(f"maxt {maxt} not in {BUCKETS}")
+    if transport.world > MAX_PEERS:
+        raise ValueError("world exceeds the device peer table")
+    cache = transport.__dict__.setdefault("_push_ws", {})
+    key = (tag, maxt)
+    if key not in cache:
+        exch = transport.alloc(
+            f"{tag}.exch{maxt}", 4 * exchange_words(transport.world, maxt)
+        )
+        if multicast is None:
+            multicast = multicast_policy(transport.world, maxt, bool(exch.mc_ptr))
+        if multicast and not exch.mc_ptr:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{tag}: multicast push requested, the {transport.kind} transport has "
+                "no multicast address"
+            )
+        ws = None
+        # local; every rank then agrees (a collective), so none waits on a failed one
+        try:
+            flags = torch.zeros(
+                maxt * CLUSTER, dtype=torch.int32, device=exch.local.device
+            )
+            ws = PushWorkspace(maxt, exch, flags, bool(multicast))
+            ws.reset()
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception(
+                "%s exchange: setup failed on rank %d", tag, transport.rank
+            )
+        transport.agree(ws is not None, f"{tag} exchange setup")
+        cache[key] = ws
+    return cache[key]
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "BUCKETS",
+    "CLUSTER",
+    "HIDDEN",
+    "K_EMPTY",
+    "PUSH_PARAMS_BYTES",
+    "PushWorkspace",
+    "bucket",
+    "exchange_words",
+    "multicast_policy",
+    "push_workspace",
+]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The MXFP8 operands of a loaded vLLM linear, in the layout the kernels read.
+
+Every kernel that reads an MXFP8 weight (front, o_proj, the MoE's shared
+expert) takes the e4m3 weight row-major `[N, K]` (N = output features) and
+its UE8M0 scales (one per 32 K elements) as the flat F8_128x4-swizzled buffer
+of `[N, K / 32]` (rows padded to 128, scale columns to a multiple of 4).
+
+What the stock MXFP8 linear kernels leave after `process_weights_after_loading`:
+
+====================================  ===================  ==================
+kernel                                `weight`           `weight_scale`
+====================================  ===================  ==================
+FlashInferCutlassMxfp8LinearKernel    [N, K] contiguous    F8_128x4, flat
+FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel    [K, N] view (the     F8_128x4, flat
+                                      transpose of a
+                                      contiguous [N, K])
+FlashInferTrtllmMxfp8LinearKernel     [N', K] shuffled     shuffled, flat
+====================================  ===================  ==================
+
+The first two hold the same bytes: the CuTe-DSL view is undone with `.t()`
+(no copy). The TRT-LLM shuffle is refused. Nothing is requantized: the e4m3
+and UE8M0 bytes are the stock layer's own.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+
+
+class Mxfp8LayoutError(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+def mxfp8_linear_nk(
+    lin: torch.nn.Module, what: str, shape: tuple[int, int] | None = None
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """(e4m3 weight [N, K] contiguous, flat uint8 F8_128x4 UE8M0 scales) of a
+    vLLM MXFP8 linear after weight processing. `shape`: the expected
+    `(N, K)`; without it, a contiguous weight is taken as `[N, K]`."""
+    w = getattr(lin, "weight", None)
+    s = getattr(lin, "weight_scale", None)
+    if w is None or s is None:
+        raise Mxfp8LayoutError(
+            f"{what}: no weight / weight_scale (not an MXFP8 linear?)"
+        )
+    w, s = w.detach(), s.detach()
+    if w.dtype != torch.float8_e4m3fn or w.dim() != 2:
+        raise Mxfp8LayoutError(
+            f"{what}: weight {w.dtype} {tuple(w.shape)}, expected 2-D float8_e4m3fn "
+            "(MXFP8)"
+        )
+    if hasattr(lin, "_mxfp8_trtllm_output_size"):
+        raise Mxfp8LayoutError(
+            f"{what}: TRT-LLM-shuffled MXFP8 weight; the kernels read the FlashInfer "
+            "CUTLASS / CuTe-DSL layout"
+        )
+    if shape is not None:
+        if tuple(w.shape) == tuple(shape):
+            pass
+        elif tuple(w.shape) == tuple(shape)[::-1]:
+            w = w.t()
+        else:
+            raise Mxfp8LayoutError(
+                f"{what}: weight {tuple(w.shape)}, expected [N, K] = {tuple(shape)} "
+                "or its [K, N] view"
+            )
+    elif not w.is_contiguous() and w.t().is_contiguous():
+        w = w.t()  # the CuTe-DSL kernel's [K, N] view
+    if not w.is_contiguous():
+        raise Mxfp8LayoutError(
+            f"{what}: weight [N, K] = {tuple(w.shape)} with strides {w.stride()} is "
+            "not row-major"
+        )
+    n, k = w.shape
+    if k % 32:
+        raise Mxfp8LayoutError(f"{what}: K = {k} is not a multiple of 32")
+    want = (n + 127) // 128 * 128 * ((k // 32 + 3) // 4 * 4)
+    sf = s.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).reshape(-1)
+    if sf.numel() != want:
+        raise Mxfp8LayoutError(
+            f"{what}: {sf.numel()} scale bytes, expected {want} (F8_128x4-swizzled "
+            f"UE8M0 of [{n}, {k // 32}])"
+        )
+    return w, sf
+
+
+__all__ = ["Mxfp8LayoutError", "mxfp8_linear_nk"]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""allreduce_norm stage: the post-attention boundary of a sparse layer (TP4).
+
+One launch (CuTe DSL `post/kernel.py` `post_route_kernel`) after the o_proj stage:
+
+1. lands the four ranks' bf16 o_proj partials the o_proj GEMV pushed into this
+   rank's boundary exchange (`_exchange.push_workspace(transport, 8, "g3")`),
+   sums them in rank order, adds the residual, Gemma RMSNorm;
+2. writes the routed experts' NVFP4 activation with the mode-Q per-token scale
+   (the M3.1 QAT FC1 row quantizer) and, optionally, an MXFP8 copy;
+3. routes: a dedicated warp polls the o_proj router CTAs' tagged partial logits
+   (`RouterExchangeSlot`), scales them by the row's 1/rms, runs the
+   MiniMax2 top-4 (sigmoid + correction bias, scaled-sum normalize x 2) and
+   publishes tagged route lines the fused MoE engine polls.
+
+The hand-off to the MoE stage is `MoeHandoff` (exact layout below).
+
+Buffers come from `_comm.PeerTransport`; every input is an explicit tensor.
+
+Why not upstream `finalize_allreduce_norm.FinalizeAllReduceGemmaRMSNormMxfp8`:
+its arithmetic (rank-order fp32 sum, bf16 residual, Gemma RMSNorm, UE8M0
+MXFP8 in the 128x4 layout) is the same contract, but its device protocol is
+different and cannot be swapped in without rewriting the producers: upstream's
+consumer reads a three-generation multicast mailbox filled by its own publish
+kernel (BF16 -0.0 sentinel), while here the producers (the o_proj GEMV and the
+fused MoE engine) push unicast into a two-parity exchange whose parity flags the
+consumer flips, and the same launch also performs routing and the NVFP4 tail.
+What is reused: the test oracle uses the same UE8M0 / 128x4 math, and
+`_comm.SymmMemPeerTransport` (the mechanism upstream uses) can provide the
+peer pointers instead of CUDA IPC.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from . import _arch
+from ._comm import PeerTransport
+from ._exchange import HIDDEN, bucket, push_workspace
+
+H = HIDDEN
+E = 128
+TOP_K = 4
+WORLD = 4  # the TP4 default
+WORLDS = (4, 8)  # the post kernel's worlds (a compile-time parameter of post/kernel.py)
+NPART = 1  # rx parts per source rank: the o_proj router CTAs push a + r as one part
+REPL = 16  # route-line replicas: engine CTA bx polls replica bx % REPL
+ROUTE_LINE_U64 = 16  # one 128-byte line per (replica, row); words 0..3 = top-4
+RCTR_STRIDE = 32  # int32 words per row counter (its own 128-byte line)
+NR = 16  # o_proj router CTAs (8 experts each)
+RX_PARITIES = 2  # router exchange halves, by tag parity (RouterExchangeSlot)
+X4_SF_ROWS = 16  # e4m3 block-scale rows of the x4 scale allocation
+X4_ROW_BYTES = H // 16  # 384
+S_T_BYTE = X4_SF_ROWS * X4_ROW_BYTES  # fp32 s_t[t] at byte 6144 + 4 t
+FC1_QAT_MAX = 6.0 * 448.0  # s_t = bf16(amax / 2688)
+EPS = 1e-6
+RX_DEADLINE_NS = 2_000_000_000  # routing warp's rx poll deadline (then __trap)
+DEFAULT_CL = 8  # CTAs per row (cluster width); 4 / 8 / 16 are instantiated
+
+# Upper bound of the post kernel's static shared memory (the largest instantiation, CL =
+# 16: csq 16 x 4 floats + warp partials + mbarrier). The exact value is read from the
+# compiled kernel by ``kernel_info``.
+POST_SMEM_BOUND = 1024
+
+
+def _ext(world: int = WORLD):
+    if world not in WORLDS:
+        raise ValueError(f"post_route: world {world} not in {WORLDS}")
+    from .post.host import post_ops
+
+    return post_ops(world)
+
+
+class RouterExchangeSlot:
+    """One layer's router exchange between its o_proj router CTAs (writers,
+    every rank's) and its post routing warp (reader, this rank).
+
+    `rx`: u64 `[2][maxt][world][NPART][E]` per rank = (tag << 32) | fp32 bits,
+    zero = no call (tags start at 1); call `tag` lives in half `tag & 1`.
+    Peer-addressable (each rank's o_proj router CTAs store into every rank's
+    slot).
+
+    Why two halves: rank A's o_proj(k + 1) stores into rank B's slot as soon
+    as A's own post(k) has finished, which needs B's o_proj(k) data but not
+    B's post(k) read, so with one buffer it could overwrite B's unread tag-k
+    words (B's post then never sees its tag and traps at the deadline). It
+    cannot get two calls ahead: A's o_proj(k + 2) waits (grid dependency) for
+    A's post(k + 1), which needs B's o_proj(k + 1) words, stored only after
+    B's post(k) finished (B's own grid dependency).
+
+    `rxc` int32 `[maxt][32]`: word 0
+    of row t = tag of the last consumed rx call (post side). `oep` int32
+    `[NR][32]`: word 0 of router CTA r = its call counter (o_proj side). Every
+    o_proj call must be followed by the post call of the same layer, or the
+    counters drift and the post traps at its deadline; `reset` re-aligns.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, transport: PeerTransport, layer_idx: int, maxt: int = 8):
+        if transport.world not in WORLDS:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"router exchange: world {transport.world} not in {WORLDS}"
+            )
+        self.transport, self.layer_idx, self.maxt = transport, layer_idx, maxt
+        self.world = transport.world
+        # u64 words of one tag-parity half
+        self.half_words = maxt * self.world * NPART * E
+        self.rx = transport.alloc(
+            f"minimax_m3_sd.rx.L{layer_idx}.t{maxt}",
+            RX_PARITIES * self.half_words * 8,
+            align=256,
+        )
+        dev = self.rx.local.device
+        self.bases = (
+            self.rx.peer_ptrs_tensor()
+        )  # int64 [MAX_PEERS], entries >= world are 0
+        self.rxc = torch.zeros(maxt * RCTR_STRIDE, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+        self.oep = torch.zeros(NR * RCTR_STRIDE, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+
+    @property
+    def rx_local(self) -> int:
+        return int(self.rx.local.data_ptr())
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        """Collective (every rank, same point, outside graph capture): zero the
+        rx words and both counters."""
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            raise RuntimeError("RouterExchangeSlot.reset during graph capture")
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        self.transport.barrier()
+        self.rx.local.zero_()
+        self.rxc.zero_()
+        self.oep.zero_()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        self.transport.barrier()
+
+
+@dataclass
+class MoeHandoff:
+    """What the post writes and the fused MoE engine reads (one per layer and
+    row count; rows = the engine's maxt, fixed at build).
+
+    =============  ======================  =========================================
+    field          dtype / shape           content
+    =============  ======================  =========================================
+    normed         bf16 [rows, 6144]       Gemma-RMSNorm output (shared-expert input)
+    residual_out   bf16 [rows, 6144]       bf16(bf16(sum partials) + residual_in)
+    x4_q           uint8 [16, 3072]        NVFP4 codes of normed rows, row-major,
+                                           low nibble = even column; rows >= rows
+                                           untouched
+    x4_sf_full     uint8 [17, 384]         rows 0..15: e4m3 block-16 scales,
+                                           row-major `[row][col / 16]`; row 16: fp32
+                                           s_t[0..95] (bytes 6144 + 4 t)
+    x4_sf          uint8 [16, 384]         view of x4_sf_full[:16]
+    x4_pts         fp32 [96]               view of x4_sf_full[16] (s_t per row)
+    x4_sfsc        fp32 [1]                1.0 (unused by mode Q; struct field)
+    route          int64 [16, rows, 16]    `[replica][row][word]`; words 0..3 =
+                                           (tag << 32) | (id << 16) | bf16(w) of
+                                           the top-4 in rank order; engine CTA bx
+                                           polls replica bx % 16 for tag ==
+                                           rctr-epoch + 1
+    rctr           int32 [rows, 32]        word 0 of row t = tag of the last
+                                           publish (post-owned)
+    mx_q, mx_sf    uint8 or None           optional MXFP8 normed (codes [rows,
+                                           6144], 128x4-swizzled UE8M0); None in M1
+    =============  ======================  =========================================
+
+    Mode Q dequant: value = e2m1(code) * e4m3(sf) * s_t (no global scale); FC1
+    is scaled by s_t per token after the GEMM; FC2 uses the fixed scale 16
+    folded into the weights (moe stage's weight prep).
+    """
+
+    rows: int
+    normed: torch.Tensor
+    residual_out: torch.Tensor
+    x4_q: torch.Tensor
+    x4_sf_full: torch.Tensor
+    x4_sf: torch.Tensor
+    x4_pts: torch.Tensor
+    x4_sfsc: torch.Tensor
+    route: torch.Tensor
+    rctr: torch.Tensor
+    mx_q: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    mx_sf: torch.Tensor | None = None
+
+    @classmethod
+    def allocate(cls, rows: int, device, mxfp8: bool = False) -> MoeHandoff:
+        if not 1 <= rows <= X4_SF_ROWS:
+            raise ValueError(f"rows {rows} outside 1..{X4_SF_ROWS}")
+        x4r = max(rows, X4_SF_ROWS)

+"""Stage `front`: the attention front of one sparse layer in one launch.
+
+The device code is CuTe DSL (`front_kernel.py`, compiled per specialisation
+at build). One cluster-of-4 grid does, per decode row:
+
+1. boundary: TP all-reduce of the previous sublayer's bf16 partials (Lamport
+   push exchange), + residual (-> `out_residual`), Gemma RMSNorm, MXFP8
+   quantization of the normed row;
+2. QKV + index-Q + index-K MXFP8 GEMV (tcgen05 `kind::mxf8f6f4`), split-K over
+   the 4 CTAs of a cluster, DSMEM reduce;
+3. epilogue: per-head Gemma RMSNorm + NeoX RoPE, bf16/FP8 Q, FP8 index-Q, FP8 K/V
+   insert into the KV cache, FP8 index-K insert into the indexer cache;
+4. optionally the step metadata of the layer (one extra cluster).
+
+Exchange modes (`prepushed`):
+
+- `False` (0): this front pushes its own partial `x` into every rank's
+  exchange, then polls. Uses the `"front"` exchange of the transport.
+- `True` (2): the producer of the previous sublayer (the fused MoE engine)
+  already pushed into the shared boundary exchange (`"g3"`, see
+  `_exchange.py`); the front only polls. `x` must be None.
+
+Every CTA of the grid spins (the GEMV clusters poll the boundary clusters'
+hand-off; the boundary polls peers), so the whole grid must be co-resident:
+the constructor checks that against the live device and raises
+`ResidencyError` otherwise.
+
+The per-rank head geometry (nq, nkv, niq) is a compile-time parameter: TP4 is
+16 / 1 / 1 (20 head clusters), TP8 8 / 1 / 1 (12 head clusters).
+
+Exchange buffers come from `_comm.PeerTransport`; cache formats are
+checked (FP8 e4m3 only; NVFP4 rejected).
+"""
+

+from dataclasses import dataclass

+@dsl_user_op
+def poll_x(pend, g0, g1, g2, g3, gw, s0, s1, s2, s3, sw, *, loc=None, ip=None):
+    """The Lamport hand-off poll of one thread: up to four 16-byte activation items (bits 0..3 of pend) and one scale
+    word (bit 4), all loaded in one round per spin; an item is accepted once none of its bytes is the sentinel (0x80
+    for activations, 0xFF for scales) and is stored to shared memory."""
+    loads = []
+    checks = []
+    for q in range(4):
+        loads.append(
+            f"and.b32 t, pend, {1 << q};\n\tsetp.ne.b32 p, t, 0;\n\t"
+            f"@p ld.volatile.global.v4.s32 {{x{q}0, x{q}1, x{q}2, x{q}3}}, [${1 + q}];\n\t"
+        )
+        chk = f"and.b32 t, pend, {1 << q};\n\tsetp.eq.b32 p, t, 0;\n\t@p bra SK{q};\n\tmov.b32 acc, 0;\n\t"
+        for j in range(4):
+            chk += (
+                f"xor.b32 t, x{q}{j}, 0x80808080;\n\tand.b32 z, t, 0x7F7F7F7F;\n\tadd.u32 z, z, 0x7F7F7F7F;\n\t"
+                "or.b32 z, z, t;\n\tnot.b32 z, z;\n\tand.b32 z, z, 0x80808080;\n\tor.b32 acc, acc, z;\n\t"
+            )
+        chk += (
+            f"setp.ne.b32 p, acc, 0;\n\t@p bra SK{q};\n\t"
+            f"st.shared.v4.b32 [${6 + q}], {{x{q}0, x{q}1, x{q}2, x{q}3}};\n\tand.b32 pend, pend, {~(1 << q) & 0xFFFFFFFF};\n\t"
+            f"SK{q}:\n\t"
+        )
+        checks.append(chk)
+    text = (
+        "{\n\t.reg .pred p;\n\t.reg .b32 pend, t, z, acc, w;\n\t.reg .b64 sp;\n\t"
+        + "".join(f".reg .b32 x{q}0, x{q}1, x{q}2, x{q}3;\n\t" for q in range(4))
+        + "mov.b32 pend, $0;\n\tmov.b64 sp, 0;\n\tPXL:\n\tsetp.eq.b32 p, pend, 0;\n\t@p bra PXD;\n\t"
+        + "".join(loads)
+        + "and.b32 t, pend, 16;\n\tsetp.ne.b32 p, t, 0;\n\t@p ld.volatile.global.u32 w, [$5];\n\t"
+        + "".join(checks)
+        + "and.b32 t, pend, 16;\n\tsetp.eq.b32 p, t, 0;\n\t@p bra SKW;\n\tnot.b32 t, w;\n\t"
+        "and.b32 z, t, 0x7F7F7F7F;\n\tadd.u32 z, z, 0x7F7F7F7F;\n\tor.b32 z, z, t;\n\tnot.b32 z, z;\n\t"
+        "and.b32 z, z, 0x80808080;\n\tsetp.ne.b32 p, z, 0;\n\t@p bra SKW;\n\tst.shared.b32 [$10], w;\n\t"
+        "and.b32 pend, pend, 0xFFFFFFEF;\n\tSKW:\n\t"
+        "add.s64 sp, sp, 1;\n\tsetp.gt.s64 p, sp, 2147483648;\n\t@p trap;\n\tbra PXL;\n\tPXD:\n\t}"
+    )
+    _asm(
+        None,
+        [
+            I32(pend),
+            I64(g0),
+            I64(g1),
+            I64(g2),
+            I64(g3),
+            I64(gw),
+            I32(s0),
+            I32(s1),
+            I32(s2),
+            I32(s3),
+            I32(sw),
+        ],
+        text,
+        "r,l,l,l,l,l,r,r,r,r,r",
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )
+

+def sdesc(saddr, lbo: int, sbo: int, layout: int):
+    """tcgen05 shared memory descriptor of a 16-byte aligned shared address."""
+    lo = I64((saddr >> I32(4)) & I32(0x3FFF))
+    return lo | I64(
+        ((lbo >> 4) & 0x3FFF) << 16
+        | ((sbo >> 4) & 0x3FFF) << 32
+        | (1 << 46)
+        | (layout << 61)
+    )
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Launch geometry of the specialized-decode kernels as a function of the SM
+count (and, for cluster kernels, of the occupancy the CUDA runtime reports).
+
+Pure Python (no torch, no CUDA), so every choice can be checked on CPU for any
+SM count. The stages call these functions with the live
+`_arch.DeviceSpec.sm_count` and the probed occupancy; nothing here is a
+substitute for the build-time residency checks in `_arch`, which still fail
+closed.
+
+Which launch dimensions depend on the SM count:
+
+=================  ==================================================  =========
+stage              grid                                                SM-bound?
+=================  ==================================================  =========
+front              4 x (heads + 1) CTAs, all spinning                  residency
+sparse_decode      rows x Hkv clusters of 16 or 8 CTAs                 width, waves
+o_proj             (6144 / 128) x 2 + 16 CTAs (shape-derived)          no
+allreduce_norm     rows clusters of `cl` CTAs, all spinning          residency
+moe                one CTA per SM: routed = SMs - shared CTAs          split
+page_topk          rows x column splits CTAs, no cross-CTA wait        no
+index_score        upstream kernel, (batch, 256) CTAs, no waits        no
+=================  ==================================================  =========
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+# Every grid below is sized from ``multiProcessorCount`` of the live device (it differs
+# between parts of one arch and shrinks under MIG or green contexts); nothing here
+# assumes a particular SM count.
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- moe:
+# shared-expert CTAs beside the routed CTAs (grid = one CTA per SM)
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+MOE_VALID_N_SHARED = (24, 48)  # what the shared tiling admits at I = 768 per rank
+MOE_MIN_ROUTED_CTAS = 64  # the fused router takes at most 2 experts per routed CTA
+MOE_MAX_ROWS = 8
+
+_H, _I, _E, _TOPK = 6144, 768, 128, 4
+# Bytes one routed CTA group streams per distinct expert (NVFP4 FC1 + FC2 values and
+# e4m3 scales per 16) and the shared CTAs stream per call (MXFP8 gate_up + down values
+# and UE8M0 scales per 32).
+MOE_ROUTED_EXPERT_BYTES = (2 * _I * _H + _H * _I) // 2 + (2 * _I * _H + _H * _I) // 16
+MOE_SHARED_EXPERT_BYTES = (2 * _I * _H + _H * _I) + (2 * _I * _H + _H * _I) // 32
+# Relative cost of one routed byte vs one shared byte on a CTA (router GEMV,
+# FC1 -> FC2 hand-off and split units are not free). On B200 and GB300 this
+# value gives 48 shared CTAs up to 2 rows and 24 above, the split the engine is
+# validated with there (engine A/B against the stock MoE, its float64
+# reference, and the decode-step measurements). A per-device sweep of the
+# split is a follow-up; measured choices go into MOE_N_SHARED_OVERRIDES.
+MOE_ROUTED_COST = 0.75
+
+# Measured overrides of the model, keyed by live SM count: rows 1..8 -> shared
+# CTAs. Empty until an A/B on hardware beats the model for some SM count; the
+# model's choice is used for every SM count not listed.
+MOE_N_SHARED_OVERRIDES: dict[int, tuple[int, ...]] = {}
+
+
+def expected_distinct_experts(rows: int, experts: int = _E, topk: int = _TOPK) -> float:
+    """E[distinct experts] of `rows` tokens choosing `topk` of `experts`
+    uniformly (the routed weight bytes a call streams scale with this)."""
+    return experts * (1.0 - (1.0 - topk / experts) ** rows)
+
+
+def moe_step_cost(
+    rows: int, sm_count: int, n_shared: int, routed_cost: float = MOE_ROUTED_COST
+) -> float:
+    """Bytes-per-CTA model of one engine call: the slower of the routed CTAs
+    (the call's distinct experts over SMs - shared CTAs) and the shared CTAs."""
+    routed_ctas = sm_count - n_shared
+    if routed_ctas <= 0:
+        return float("inf")
+    routed = (
+        routed_cost
+        * expected_distinct_experts(rows)
+        * MOE_ROUTED_EXPERT_BYTES
+        / routed_ctas
+    )
+    return max(routed, MOE_SHARED_EXPERT_BYTES / n_shared)
+
+
+def moe_n_shared_model(
+    rows: int, sm_count: int, routed_cost: float = MOE_ROUTED_COST
+) -> int:
+    """The valid shared-CTA count with the lowest modelled cost (ties: more
+    shared CTAs) that leaves at least `MOE_MIN_ROUTED_CTAS` routed CTAs."""
+    ok = [s for s in MOE_VALID_N_SHARED if sm_count - s >= MOE_MIN_ROUTED_CTAS]
+    if not ok:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"moe: {sm_count} SMs cannot hold {MOE_MIN_ROUTED_CTAS} routed CTAs beside "
+            f"{min(MOE_VALID_N_SHARED)} shared CTAs"
+        )
+    return min(ok, key=lambda s: (moe_step_cost(rows, sm_count, s, routed_cost), -s))
+
+
+def moe_n_shared(rows: int, sm_count: int) -> int:
+    """Shared-expert CTAs of the engine for `rows` tokens on `sm_count`
+    (live) SMs: the model, unless a measured override exists for that count."""
+    if not 1 <= rows <= MOE_MAX_ROWS:
+        raise ValueError(f"moe: rows {rows} outside 1..{MOE_MAX_ROWS}")
+    tab = MOE_N_SHARED_OVERRIDES.get(sm_count)
+    nsh = tab[rows - 1] if tab is not None else moe_n_shared_model(rows, sm_count)
+    if sm_count - nsh < MOE_MIN_ROUTED_CTAS:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"moe: {sm_count} SMs leave {sm_count - nsh} routed CTAs beside {nsh} "
+            "shared"
+        )
+    return nsh
+
+
+def moe_routed_ctas(rows: int, sm_count: int, n_shared: int | None = None) -> int:
+    """Routed CTAs of the engine: every SM not running a shared CTA."""
+    nsh = moe_n_shared(rows, sm_count) if n_shared is None else n_shared
+    return sm_count - nsh
+
+
+def moe_fc2_blocks_per_cta(routed_ctas: int) -> int:
+    """FC2 32-row output blocks per routed CTA, ceil(6144 / 32 / routed); the
+    engine's shared-memory budget was sized for at most 2."""
+    return -(-(_H // 32) // routed_ctas)
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# sparse_decode: cluster width per (rows, KV heads)
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+SPARSE_CLUSTER_SIZES = (16, 8)  # instantiated widths, widest first
+# From this many (row, KV head) clusters on, use 8-CTA clusters even when 16 would fit
+# (the wave count matters more there than the shorter per-CTA page loop of 16). Applies
+# to the one-wave rows only.
+SPARSE_WIDE_CLUSTERS = 32
+
+
+def sparse_waves(
+    rows: int, num_kv_heads: int, cl: int, max_active_clusters: Mapping[int, int]
+) -> float:
+    """Waves of `rows` x `num_kv_heads` clusters of width `cl` (inf if
+    that width is not schedulable)."""
+    n = max_active_clusters.get(cl, 0)
+    return float("inf") if n < 1 else -(-(rows * num_kv_heads) // n)
+
+
+def sparse_cluster_size(
+    rows: int,
+    num_kv_heads: int,
+    max_active_clusters: Mapping[int, int] | None = None,
+    *,
+    one_wave: bool = True,
+) -> int:
+    """Cluster width of the sparse decode for `rows` x `num_kv_heads`
+    clusters. The preferred width is 16 below `SPARSE_WIDE_CLUSTERS`
+    clusters, else 8. With `max_active_clusters` (width -> clusters the
+    device holds at once, `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters`):
+
+    - `one_wave`: the first width, from the preferred one down, whose grid
+      is co-resident; `ValueError` if none is (fail closed);
+    - otherwise the grid only has to be schedulable: the width with the
+      fewest waves, the wider one on a tie (more CTAs per row, shorter
+      per-CTA page loop); `ValueError` if no width is schedulable."""
+    need = rows * num_kv_heads
+    if need <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("sparse_decode: rows and KV heads must be positive")
+    pref = 16 if need < SPARSE_WIDE_CLUSTERS else 8
+    if max_active_clusters is None:
+        return pref
+    if one_wave:
+        for cl in (c for c in SPARSE_CLUSTER_SIZES if c <= pref):
+            if max_active_clusters.get(cl, 0) >= need:
+                return cl
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"sparse_decode: {need} clusters do not fit in one wave at any width "
+            f"(device holds {dict(max_active_clusters)})"
+        )
+    best = min(
+        SPARSE_CLUSTER_SIZES,
+        key=lambda c: (sparse_waves(rows, num_kv_heads, c, max_active_clusters), -c),
+    )
+    if sparse_waves(rows, num_kv_heads, best, max_active_clusters) == float("inf"):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "sparse_decode: no cluster width is schedulable "
+            f"({dict(max_active_clusters)})"
+        )
+    return best
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "MOE_N_SHARED_OVERRIDES",
+    "MOE_VALID_N_SHARED",
+    "expected_distinct_experts",
+    "moe_fc2_blocks_per_cta",
+    "moe_n_shared",
+    "moe_n_shared_model",
+    "moe_routed_ctas",
+    "moe_step_cost",
+    "sparse_cluster_size",
+    "sparse_waves",
+]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""index_score stage: decode-time index page scores, served by upstream
+vLLM's `minimax_m3_index_decode_score_cutedsl`
+(`vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/ops/index_decode_score.py`).
+
+Upstream reuse, no port: that CuTe DSL kernel accepts an FP8 E4M3 index query
+and an FP8 E4M3 index-K cache ([pages, 128, D], unscaled e4m3, as written by
+upstream's `MiniMaxM3IndexerCache` for `indexer_kv_dtype="fp8"`) and
+writes fp32 page scores by strides, so it serves the fp8 indexer path of the
+specialized decode as is. Its grid is (batch, split_k = 256) and it does not
+spin, so it needs no residency check.
+
+NVFP4 index caches are rejected (`_dtypes`); the upstream NVFP4 index path
+is a different kernel and a different cache layout.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+from . import _dtypes
+
+PAGE = 128
+# Rows of the largest launch: the grid is per request, so rows only bound the executor's
+# largest step (8 requests x qlen 8).
+MAX_ROWS = 64
+# CTAs per request of the scorer grid (batch, split_k); the scores do not depend on it.
+# Upstream's wrapper uses 256, which the steps of up to SPLIT_MIN_ROWS rows (one request
+# at K = 7) keep. With two or more requests the grid is batch-fastest, so a long
+# request's CTAs are every batch-th block and land on a fraction of the SMs; a larger
+# split spreads them (768 measured faster for a long request next to a short one).
+UPSTREAM_SPLIT_K = 256
+SPLIT_MIN_ROWS = 8
+SPLIT_K_MULTI = 768
+
+
+def split_k_for(rows: int) -> int:
+    """The scorer split of a step of `rows` rows."""
+    return UPSTREAM_SPLIT_K if rows <= SPLIT_MIN_ROWS else SPLIT_K_MULTI
+
+
+class StockIndexScoreStage:
+    """`__call__(idx_q, index_cache, block_table, seq_lens, score_out, *,
+    decode_query_len)`
+
+    idx_q        e4m3 [batch * qlen, H_idx, D]   (H_idx per rank; H_idx * max_qlen <= 32)
+    index_cache  e4m3 [pages, 128, D]
+    block_table  int32 [batch, max_pages]
+    seq_lens     int32 [batch]
+    score_out    float32 [H_idx, batch * qlen, >= max_pages] (may be a transposed view of
+                 upstream `unified_scores[:nd]`)
+    """  # noqa: E501
+
+    stage = "index_score"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        num_index_heads: int,
+        max_decode_query_len: int,
+        indexer_kv_dtype: str = "fp8",
+        max_rows: int = MAX_ROWS,
+    ):
+        # Rejects nvfp4 (and anything without a kernel here) with a clear error.
+        self.fmt = _dtypes.indexer_cache_format(indexer_kv_dtype)
+        if num_index_heads * max_decode_query_len > 32:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"index_score: {num_index_heads} index heads x qlen "
+                f"{max_decode_query_len} > 32 "
+                "(the upstream CuTe DSL decode-score tile)"
+            )
+        self.num_index_heads = int(num_index_heads)
+        self.max_decode_query_len = int(max_decode_query_len)
+        self.max_rows = int(max_rows)
+        self._fn: Any = None
+        self._kernels: dict[
+            int, Any
+        ] = {}  # split_k -> compiled kernel (not upstream's 256)
+
+    def build(self):
+        from vllm.models.minimax_m3.nvidia.ops.index_decode_score import (
+            minimax_m3_index_decode_score_cutedsl,
+        )
+
+        self._fn = minimax_m3_index_decode_score_cutedsl
+        import torch
+
+        from vllm.models.minimax_m3.nvidia.ops.index_decode_score import (
+            _TORCH_TO_CUTE_DTYPE,
+            IndexDecodeScoreKernel,
+        )
+
+        # Compile every split the row counts use now, not inside a capture.
+        for sk in {split_k_for(r) for r in range(1, self.max_rows + 1)} - {
+            UPSTREAM_SPLIT_K
+        }:
+            self._kernels[sk] = IndexDecodeScoreKernel.compile(
+                _TORCH_TO_CUTE_DTYPE[torch.float8_e4m3fn],
+                self.num_index_heads,
+                self.max_decode_query_len,
+                sk,
+                128,
+            )
+        return self
+
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        idx_q,
+        index_cache,
+        block_table,
+        seq_lens,
+        score_out,
+        *,
+        decode_query_len: int,
+    ):
+        import torch
+
+        if self._fn is None:
+            self.build()
+        if idx_q.shape[0] > self.max_rows:
+            raise ValueError(f"index_score: {idx_q.shape[0]} rows > {self.max_rows}")
+        if idx_q.dtype != torch.float8_e4m3fn:
+            raise TypeError(f"index_score: fp8 index query expected, got {idx_q.dtype}")
+        _dtypes.check_cache_tensor("indexer K", index_cache, self.fmt)
+        if index_cache.dtype != torch.float8_e4m3fn:
+            index_cache = index_cache.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        if index_cache.dim() != 3 or index_cache.shape[1] != PAGE:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "index_score: index cache [pages, 128, D] expected, got "
+                f"{tuple(index_cache.shape)}"
+            )
+        kernel = self._kernels.get(split_k_for(idx_q.shape[0]))
+        if kernel is not None:
+            if idx_q.shape[0] != block_table.shape[0] * int(decode_query_len):
+                raise ValueError("index_score: rows != batch x decode_query_len")
+            kernel(idx_q, index_cache, block_table, score_out, seq_lens)
+            return score_out
+        return self._fn(
+            idx_q,
+            index_cache,
+            block_table,
+            seq_lens,
+            0,  # max_seq_len: unused by the CuTe DSL kernel
+            0,  # init_blocks: unused (forced pages are page_topk's job)
+            0,  # local_blocks: unused
+            1,  # num_kv_heads: unused
+            int(decode_query_len),
+            self.max_decode_query_len,
+            score_out,
+        )
+
+
+__all__ = ["StockIndexScoreStage"]
